paragraphs:
Idi (or Rav Idi). R. Yosef said, “Idi recited”; Rava said, “Idi explained it to me,” Kiddushin 40a; Nedarim 5b. Rashi, Bava Metzia 8b: a sage’s name. But Eizehu Neshekh 74b has Rava say, “Rabbi Idi explained it to me”; Rashi likewise has Rav Idi. Rava said in Rabbi Idi’s name; in Rabbi Chanina’s name, Eruvin 57b; in Rabbi Shimon’s name; in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 1.
[Glosses: Idi. (a) Bava Metzia 74, end of b: Rava said, “Rav Idi explained it to me,” as in Rashi. It seems to me that the word “and Rav” [ורב] is erroneous; the new editions did not correct it. (b) Chagigah 5, end of b: Rabbi Idi, father of Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, regularly, etc. Ein Yaakov reads Rav Idi, son of Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, regularly, etc. Rashi has Rabbi Yaakov regularly, as do the new editions. I think it should read Rav Idi regularly.]
